name: Software Quality Fundamentals
summary: Testing is not hunting for defects at the end: it is deciding what is worth checking, and when.
prerequisites: No programming required. This is the entry point of the Quality track.
syllabus: What quality assurance is and what it is not
The tester’s mindset: systematic doubt, not suspicion
Testing approaches: black, grey and white box
Lifecycle models: waterfall, V, spiral and agile
Methodologies: TDD, BDD, ATDD and root cause analysis
Test oracles and prioritisation: where to start when time runs short
topics: What quality assurance is: preventing versus detecting
Product quality and process quality
The cost of a defect across the lifecycle: why finding it early is cheaper
The tester’s mindset: hypothesis, evidence and reproduction
The QA role on the team: not the guardian of "you cannot ship"
Black box: testing by behaviour
White box: testing with knowledge of the code
Grey box: the middle ground people actually use
The waterfall and V models: testing as a mirror of the requirement
The spiral model and iterative development
The agile model: the role of testing in a short cycle
Scrum: ceremonies, definition of done and testing inside the sprint
Kanban: flow, work-in-progress limits and continuous quality
XP and SAFe: what changes for the tester
Test-driven development (TDD): red, green, refactor
Behaviour-driven development (BDD): Gherkin and a shared language
Acceptance test-driven development (ATDD)
Root cause analysis: the five whys and the Ishikawa diagram
The test oracle: how you know the result is correct
Prioritisation: risk, impact, usage frequency and defect history
Entry and exit criteria for a test cycle
Useful metrics and metrics that turn into theatre
